title: Consolidate shared runtime utilities and tolerances
description:
Source: docs/tasks/tickets/CC-090-common-utility-and-tolerance-consolidation.md
Source key: CC-090

## Summary

Consolidate only mechanically identical runtime finite-validation helpers without moving hierarchy or domain semantics into Common.

## Scope

- Centralize exact finite checks for scalar, Vector3, and Quaternion values.
- Preserve domain-owned curve, gradient, thickness, quantization, mirror, tolerance, ID-ordering, PartType, sibling-order, and hierarchy semantics.
- Do not add adapter base classes, generic services, or speculative frameworks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- NumericValidity is the shared owner for the verified scalar, Vector3, and Quaternion finite checks.
- Definition, canonicalization, projection, curve, gradient, and thickness call sites retain behavior and use the shared finite checks where contracts are identical.
- Existing definition, serialization, projection, appearance, mirror, and editor tests remain green.
- Deferred utility families are not represented as completed work without a separate call-site inventory and evidence.

## Validation

Unity 6000.0.35f1 focused PlayMode validation passed 108/108 tests across definition, serialization, body projection, and body appearance fixtures. Runtime build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors. Future utility families require new evidence before scope expansion.

## Findings

The audit found repeated finite checks plus broader utility candidates. The finite checks were mechanically identical; the remaining candidates have not been claimed as part of this completed slice.

## Blockers

None for the completed finite-check scope. TSK-0093 owns hierarchy mechanics.

## Next Step

Keep Done for the finite-check scope. Reopen only if a concrete mechanically-identical utility family is inventoried and accepted as a new scope decision.
